newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss mutual fund assets jump 26 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Swiss mutual fund assets jump 26 percent in 1996.

text.p: Assets of Switzerland's mutual funds grew by 26 percent in 1996, buoyed by rising demand from hungry clients, a new survey showed.

Combined assets of public mutual funds set up by Swiss banks at home and abroad grew to 232.4 billion Swiss Francs ($166 billion) at the end of 1996, up 48 billion over a year ago, the survey by Swiss mutual fund statistician Bopp ISB said.
Mutual fund business is expanding in Switzerland as many banks try to build innovative niches in the industry.
In a departure from their traditional image as bankers for the very rich, private banks are also aggressively selling funds to a smaller, more risk-averse pool of capital.
Data on the total volume of assets managed is not published in Switzerland, a by-product of its culture of bank secrecy, and bank annual reports provide only scanty information.
But total assets under management are estimated at well over 1.2 trillion Swiss Francs ($860 billion). Bank Julius Baer estimates they will grow to 2 trillion by 2000.
The Bopp ISB survey covers only public funds and not inhouse funds managed by private banks which do not publish any data on such assets worth many billions of Swiss Francs, bankers said.
It also excludes foreign groups selling mutual funds in Switzerland such as Fidelity, Flemings, Citibank and Nomura.

The survey said net cash flow into public funds including money market, equity, bond and asset allocation funds totalled 17.6 billion Swiss Francs ($12.5 billion) in 1996 -- an average monthly net flow 1.5 billion Swiss Francs.
The market leader, Swiss Bank Corporation, held 30 percent of all industry assets with 69 billion Swiss Francs, an increase of more than 20 percent in combined assets over 1995.
It was followed by the Union Bank of Switzerland with 26 percent of the market and combined assets of 60 billion Swiss Francs at the end of 1996, up 25 percent over a year ago.
Credit Suisse Bank maintained its market share of 24 percent with combined assets of 54.5 billion Swiss Francs.
Performance data, currency denomination and asset breakdowns were not available.

But a previous survey dated November 1996 said that Swiss funds distributed in Luxembourg accounted for 68 percent of the total assets, followed by those in Switzerland with 31 percent and elsewhere in the world with 2.5 percent.
Funds distributed in Switzerland had 41 percent of assets invested in stock funds, 34 percent in bond funds, 14 percent in asset allocation funds and 12 percent in real estate funds.
Those distributed in Luxembourg had 59 percent of assets in money market funds, 24 percent in bond funds, 10 percent in asset allocation funds and seven percent in stock funds.
